text:
ana_cs: Hey team — raising from support: customer cust_82X sees duplicate full outputs (and duplicate billing) when their browser reconnects quickly during an SSE stream. They get a short partial chunk, then after reconnect the full response arrives again. They provided logs and a short recording.

mike_eng: can you paste the minimal repro/logs here? any idempotency header used by client?

ana_cs: attaching clipped server log and client timeline (transcribed):
- t=0 client opens SSE /v1/stream?model=redwood-large session_token=abc123
- t=1 partial chunk "Hello, this is a" arrives then connection drops
- t=1.1 client immediately reconnects with a new websocket/sse session_token=abc123_r1 (no X-Idempotency-Key)
- t=1.3 server sends full completion "Hello, this is a test response with details..." again
- Customer charged twice for two completions in billing export window

sophie_sre: quick glance at logs — I see resume tokens and new session ids being treated as independent requests. Server emits new generation id when session_token changes. Log excerpt: ```
[2026-03-01T12:00:05Z] INFO  stream.start session=abc123 user=cust_82X -> gen_id=gen_456 partial=true
[2026-03-01T12:00:05Z] ERROR stream.disconnect session=abc123 reason=client_proto_error
[2026-03-01T12:00:05Z] INFO  stream.start session=abc123_r1 user=cust_82X -> gen_id=gen_789 partial=false
[2026-03-01T12:00:05Z] WARN  billing.charge user=cust_82X gen=gen_456 amount=0.12
[2026-03-01T12:00:06Z] WARN  billing.charge user=cust_82X gen=gen_789 amount=0.12
```
Looks like server can't correlate reconnection to previous in-progress generation because the client created a fresh session_token. No X-Idempotency-Key present to tie requests together.

mike_eng: thanks. Can you share the exact client reconnect sequence? often clients do:```
GET /v1/stream?session=abc123  (SSE)
-- receives chunk, then socket closes
GET /v1/stream?session=abc123_r1 
```
If session param differs, server treats as new user request. If client instead reuses session token or includes the same idempotency key header, we can safely resume/deduplicate.

ana_cs: customer says their frontend library auto-creates a fresh session token on reconnect (socket manager lib). They didn't explicitly set an idempotency header.

sophie_sre: repro steps for eng:
1) start SSE without X-Idempotency-Key, session=foo
2) after first chunk, forcibly close connection client-side
3) immediately reconnect creating session=foo_v2
4) observe two completed generation events in server logs and two separate billing charges

mike_eng: quick patch plan:
- short-term: add server-side 5s sliding dedupe window keyed by (user_id, prompt_hash). If a new gen starts within window and prompt_hash matches an in-flight gen, mark it as duplicate and avoid billing.
- medium: enforce/recommend client behavior: require reuse of session_token OR provide X-Idempotency-Key header for streaming resumable requests. Update docs + SDK.
- long: change protocol to include resume_token in reconnect, validate seq offsets so reconnections always reattach to same gen if within TTL.

ana_cs: customer is asking for reversal on two duplicate charges. Can we refund?

sophie_sre: we can create a refund once eng flags the two gen_ids as duplicates in the billing ledger. I'll hold on creating a formal billing incident until eng confirms detection logic.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1234 — duplicate-billing-on-fast-reconnect. Priority: P2. Assigned to mike_eng.

mike_eng: I'll take it. First steps: add diagnostic metrics for "duplicate_gen_detected"; instrument code path that creates gen_id to emit existing_prompt_hash if present. Also add a guard to avoid double billing for gen_ids sharing the same prompt_hash within 10s and same user.

ana_cs: Customer wants temporary mitigation for their account now — can you mark future reconnections within 10s as non-billable for cust_82X while we patch?

sophie_sre: yep we can add an account-scoped flag to billing pipeline to ignore duplicate gen billing for the next 24h. Send me the gen_ids and timestamps and I'll queue refund once eng marks them duplicates.

mike_eng: repro note for the team: sample curl to show bad client behavior (no idempotency):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&session=tmp_sess"
# close connection, then
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&session=tmp_sess_r1"
```
Fix demo (reuse idempotency):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Idempotency-Key: abc-123" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&session=tmp_sess"
# reconnect using same header
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Idempotency-Key: abc-123" 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&session=tmp_sess_r1"
```
Server should detect same idempotency key and dedupe generation/billing.

mike_eng: I'll open a PR with the 5s dedupe guard + metrics. ETA 3h for PR, deploy safe patch to staging, 6-8h to prod behind feature flag.

ana_cs: thanks — please post PR and staging link here so I can test with the customer. :pray:

sophie_sre: created temporary billing ignore for cust_82X and queued manual refund for gen_456/gen_789. I'll wait for eng confirmation before finalizing.

mike_eng: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/infra/+/PR-8345 (staging deploy link in CI). Will follow up when staging is green.

ana_cs: confirmed with customer — they can pause their traffic while we validate on staging. keeping thread updated.
